To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

extended training of rats on a runway task given 0, 5, 10, and 20-seconds delay of reinforcement produced no differences in terminal speed to goal acquisition, and only minor differences in run speed.

1) extended training of rats on delayed reinforcement schedules does not produce any significant differences in the acquisition goal speeds, and 2) the 20-seconds delayed group showed a slower run speed during the first 100 trials than the other three groups.
the acquisition of a runway response is not influenced by the length of the delay of reinforcement.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of delayed reinforcement in a runway task.
the effects of extended training on delayed reinforcement.
the role of delay of reinforcement in acquisition and performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
delayed reinforcement is a variable of importance in learning and that it is a variable which should be considered in any model of learning.
the extended training of rats on a delayed reinforcement schedule does not produce any significant effects.
delayed reinforcement has no significant effects on acquisition of a simple runway task.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the delay-of-reinforcement effect does not seem to be an all-or-none effect, but is more a matter of degree.
extended training does not affect the acquisition of a delayed-reinforcement task.
the role of delayed reinforcement is to increase the rate of acquisition of the goal response and not to increase terminal goal speed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the role of extended delay training in acquisition is an open question.
extended training may be a necessary component of the study of delayed reinforcement, especially if one is interested in asymptotic performance.
extended training may be necessary to obtain a stable measure of delayed reinforcement.
